Code example

Build a labeling quality control system

intermediate coding

Implement inter-annotator agreement metrics (Cohen kappa, Fleiss kappa) and a system that flags low-quality labels for re-annotation.

What to notice

  • Kappa = (observed - expected) / (1 - expected)
  • Expected agreement assumes independence: P(both yes) + P(both no)
  • Flag items where no label gets >= threshold agreement

Expected outcome

Kappa around 0.4-0.6 (moderate agreement); several items flagged for re-annotation

Reference solution 
import numpy as np
from typing import List

def cohens_kappa(annotator1: List[int], annotator2: List[int]) -> float:
    n = len(annotator1)
    observed_agree = sum(a == b for a, b in zip(annotator1, annotator2)) / n
    p1_pos = sum(annotator1) / n
    p2_pos = sum(annotator2) / n
    expected_agree = p1_pos * p2_pos + (1 - p1_pos) * (1 - p2_pos)
    if expected_agree == 1:
        return 1.0
    return (observed_agree - expected_agree) / (1 - expected_agree)

def flag_disagreements(annotations: List[List[int]], threshold: float = 0.67) -> List[int]:
    n_items = len(annotations[0])
    flagged = []
    for i in range(n_items):
        votes = [a[i] for a in annotations]
        majority_pct = max(votes.count(0), votes.count(1)) / len(votes)
        if majority_pct < threshold:
            flagged.append(i)
    return flagged
